title: Petroleum refining
extract: Petroleum refining turns crude oil into useful products such as petrol, diesel, kerosene, and cooking gas. A refinery heats and separates crude oil in a process called fractional distillation. Nigeria’s Dangote Refinery is one of the largest single-train refineries in the world and aims to process hundreds of thousands of barrels of crude oil per day. For students, the key ideas are: crude oil is a mixture, fractions boil at different temperatures, and local refining can change fuel supply and prices. In commerce and economics class, a large refinery also links to import substitution, employment, and energy security — not to stock-trading tips.
description: chemistry and economics for secondary students
note: Trend angle: Dangote refinery in the news → teach refining + supply, not shares/investment advice
